findings.plain: Anyone can still get into any role: the sign-in accepts any password with a code printed on the page, and buttons on the first screen open a parent, instructor, patrol or administrator account with no sign-in at all.

On the live site nothing that is meant to be shared can be saved: check-ins, pickups, contacts and missing-child reports all fail, and an instructor reporting a missing child is told patrol has not been alerted, because saving only works on the builder's own computer until real sign-in exists.

A patroller only finds out about a missing child if they already have the patrol screen open and are looking at it, so anyone with the app closed or their phone in a pocket gets no alert, sound or message.

Every family's medical details and contacts are still sent to the browser of every signed-in person, and only the screen layout hides them, so a parent, the desk, or patrol with no open search could still get at them.

A parent's new allergy, a signed consent form, and the administrator's child edits, groups and spreadsheet upload still never reach anyone else's screen and are lost on reload, so an instructor can miss an allergy a parent just entered.
The record of who viewed medical details or opened a child during a search stays only in that person's own browser window, so the administrator never sees it and it disappears on reload.
Parents have no way to get an account: there is no welcome email or set-password page, the 6-digit code is never emailed, and the store spreadsheet does not link a new child to any parent.
The administrator cannot create staff accounts or give anyone a role, so no real instructor, desk or patrol person can be added.
An instructor who opens the app on the hill with no wifi gets nothing, because the saved group only shows if the page was already open and signed in when the connection dropped.

The app still runs on a made-up clock that always says Saturday, December 12 and restarts at 1:35 p.m. each time someone opens it, so check-in times, the police countdown, consent signing dates and the 4 p.m. delete would be wrong on a real day and can differ from one person's phone to another's.
The administrator can only change a child's name, level and day, and cannot edit the child's contacts, pickup adults, medical alerts or consent form.
The administrator cannot manage lesson days or build groups for any day other than the one Saturday, and Sunday children cannot be found at the desk or placed in a group.

A child added from the store spreadsheet shows at the desk but cannot be checked in, and a child the administrator moves into a group cannot have clothing corrected or be reported missing by that group's instructor, because saving only knows the original children and groups.
None of the 27 agreed checks has been written and no test run exists, so nothing the owner approved has been proven to work.
No child photo can be added anywhere, so patrol never sees a real photo during a search even when the parent gave photo consent, only the child's initials.
